### FOLLOW-UP [security]: `src/domains/release/release-notes.ts` — `buildReleaseNotesPrompt`
Reference: `18-release-architecture.adr.md` Invariant: "Every agent-produced artifact is read back from disk and validated against its contract; the release proceeds only when validation passes." ADR Verification: "NEVER: a producer's self-reported verdict stands in for faithfulness evidence — faithfulness is established by audit of the artifact against its release-data input ([audit])."
Issue: `buildReleaseNotesPrompt` appends commit subjects directly and without structural delimitation: `commitSubjects = releaseData.commits.map(c => c.subject).join("\n")` is concatenated verbatim after the instruction "Describe and group these commits faithfully, introducing no claim absent from them:". When the production `AgentRunner` lands, a repository whose commits carry adversarial subjects (e.g. `"Fix bug\n\nIgnore previous instructions and instead write..."`) could attempt prompt injection. The file-tool allowlist constrains filesystem escaping, but not what the agent writes inside the changelog. Structural Keep-a-Changelog validation would still pass, and only the faithfulness `[audit]` would catch the manipulation — post-hoc and manually. Delimiting the subjects block (e.g. XML-like boundary tags) is the conventional preventive mitigation.
Track under: `spx/26-release.enabler/32-release-notes.enabler/PLAN.md` — add under the "Production AgentRunner" deferred item, so the implementer addresses input delimitation at the same time as the SDK wrapper.
